title: This week
body:
Softmax

- Pipelined exact division and packed readback reduced RTL latency to 228 cycles at 75 MHz.
- Board latency: 5.088 µs per 49-score row, including launch/polling/readback — 5.8% lower than HPS INT8 (5.404 µs).
- All 23520 tested bytes matched HPS INT8. Relative RMSE vs FP32: 6.56%; top-1 agreement: 3/3 validation images.

LayerNorm

- Shared reciprocal and overlapped processing reduced RTL latency to 472 cycles at 75 MHz, with in-place writeback.
- Board latency: 6.362 µs per 192-channel token (24-token batch average; no timed readback) — 84.3% lower than exact-corrected HPS INT8 (40.487 µs).
- All 55296 tested bytes matched HPS INT8. Relative RMSE vs FP32: 3.49%; top-1 agreement: 3/3 validation images.

Separate bitstreams; inputs pre-staged. These are operator measurements, not full-model speedup or dataset accuracy. [Detailed results and resources](#/files/softmax-layernorm-results-2026-11-25). [Softmax and LayerNorm results — Google Doc](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1BJWlElhnC0bZsdeUpyY6uXx77ySFmQKufp9jSJVZS2Q/edit?tab=t.0).

TinyViT-5M integration — Stephanie (Yixin)

- At 90 MHz, the hybrid pipeline averages 706.09 ms per warmed inference: 1.689× faster than original FP32 CPU (1,192.68 ms) and 1.456× faster than mixed W8A8 CPU (1,028.36 ms).
- Top-1 on the same 200 labeled images: 153/200 FP32, 155/200 mixed CPU, 154/200 hybrid.
- FPGA offload covers 40 static-weight GEMMs in 454 jobs per image, including eight resident FC1→GELU→FC2 pairs. Dynamic attention stays on the HPS.
- Fitted resources: 76% ALMs, 40% DSPs, 77% M10Ks.
- [Full timing table and overview](#/files/tinyvit-5m-90mhz-timing-2026-11-26). The same Files & Data page also has the operation map and fitted resources.
